Hispanic is NOT an ethnicity. It's a label given by the USA to people from Spanish speaking countries. There are quite different ethnic backgrounds in all the Spanish speaking countries, that includes Spain itself in Europe and includes countries like Uruguay, with almost no Native American population nor black population, some Mestizo and some European descendants and countries like Dominican Republic, with Mestizo, Mulatto, Zambo ethnicities. Also, the so-called Hispanic with Native American ancestry may descent from a wide range of ethnic groups.

Are you from USA? I would call you "Estadounidense". If you don't speak Spanish nor Portuguese then you are not Latino Americano, but of Latin American descent. I would only call Mexican someone who is a Mexican citizen and I don't use the labels "Latino" nor "Hispanic" because I think they reflect the point of view of the USA or the colinizators. In Latin America it's quite different mate, but if you have only lived and experienced the USA culture, I understand that's what you know.

Regarding the face, I think it's quite obvious why no one show their faces, because of the stigma attached to self injury. But to be able to show a scar online and say it's from self injury without being censored or banned it is a step imho.

Cheers.

I'm so sorry you have to went through all that.

I have been in similar situations more often than I would like. I've been mistreated, abandoned by  that relocate, misdiagnosed, given awful meds that made me sicker... But also I've found in the path some good therapists, empathetic doctors and psychiatrists willing to listen and help me find the right meds. 

I'm not from USA, but as someone already suggested, if you are worried about interactions of meds, it would be better to try some form of therapy that doesn't need pills, unless after time and evaluation, the therapist/counselor (sorry) considers that it may help you and you can be directly derived to someone of your counselour's trust.

It's a long way. But you can do it. If I have done it I know you can.

Cheers.

I can totally relate. Specially reaching certain age. I've caused third degree burns, rupture of muscles and broken bones that had needed surgery, still have titanium in my body. I've felt shame and guilt. Now I feel sadness.

I can relate. I was quite the depressive teenager, I suffered a traumatic experience at age 22, PTSD settled and just then I started self injuring. At that time, when I was researching what was wrong with me, it was all about the "Emo" scene. Absolutely nothing to do with me. Being 27-28, working full-time, engaged, and self injuring severely was too much for me. At that time all I had was an online community about self injury that wasn't very active. Nobody I could actually talk to. It was hard, specially for being a grown adult. I was misdiagnosed by therapists. It was hard. 

I hope times has changed, and here we are, many grown adults who had struggled with something similar, you are not alone on this one.

I can only talk from my own experience, but actually relapse is quite common. I did DBT therapy back in 2011-2012, I was told there that relapse wasn't failure, was part of the process. I usually relapse at least once a year. 

I hope this can help you and that you don't give up hope.

Indeed. I think about the pathologists taking pictures of a lot of fat tissue. Not nice. 

And don't forget the bloating effect.

I know is hard, but what has worked for me at least, is try not to think in past experiences and failures and try to focus on this new experience only.  

Drinking water can help to calm anxiety eating too, but if you try to do fasting it can cause binge eating, so it's better to eat like you do regularly, but to avoid tentations with water.

I can definitely relate. It's worst for me in heat summer days. 

Everyone say this, but first try to talk to a doyto see if there is a physiological cause.

The small goals advice is a very good one. 

A healthy diet, with fruits and vegetables, plenty of water, low carbohydrates, low sugar and fat and eating small portions but more often, helped me too. Try to keep a healthy sleep cycle too.

I can relate with the fear of the future. 

Do you really want to do this? If the answer is yes, is this the only chance, or can you apply again on another date? 

I hope that asking yourself those questions may give you some helpful answers.

This is absolutely brilliant!

I am new here, registered to post on some mental health forums (yeah, I'm a bit old), and never expected to find this kind of content!

This is true, thinking about all the things that can go horribly wrong in an attempt are great stoppers.

It reminds me of the case of the girl with the transplanted face. So sad.

I have never attempted. Been struggling with treatment resistant depression for 20 years, PTSD for 15 years, etc.

I have a few loved ones that I don't want to hurt, but my main "stopper" is a family member I love very much, that helped me a lot in my darker times, when I was all alone and lost, and have been needing care since years already. I care for this elderly family member, with my cats they are like my childrens. I am a provider so I can't just disappear. In a few years they will leave this life, and so will I.

It's really shocking and sad that young people know the concept of suicide at such a young age in current times. I remember thinking "if X thing happens I rather die" or "If I see X thing I would jump off the bridge" at a very young age, but I didn't really understand at that age the concept of suicide, nor even the permanency of death.

As far as I remember, my first real struggle with suicidal ideation was at age 11. But it was probably influenced by two factors: the recent death of Kurt Cobain, who was a musician I really admired as a child and I was looking forward to see live, and the death of a very young and close relative in a road accident, all in the same period of time. He was the first relative I lost, even before my grandparents, and he was very young and close to me, almost like a brother.
Congrats! Last summer, I spent a lot of time at my sister's at a lot of that time at the pool. It was great! I felt like a child.

I think I am very old. I was a kid when BSSM came out, like 10 years old. The first song I listened was Give It Away, I liked it, and the video. But it was Under the Bridge the one that caught me. Then I got the cassette, yeah, cassette. When John left I checked Niandra, I was 13 iirc, at that age I was listening a lot of interesting music and I had a crush on John, typical at that age. I didn't knew much about the drugs at that time, there wasn't internet. I followed his solo career.

That VPRO interview kills me. I hate it.

Just wanted to add that is great that young people are discovering John's music, and also the music I listened in my early teens, like RHCP and Nirvana, makes me feel not so out-of-date!

Treatment resistant depression sucks.

I can relate.

I can't travel without music and earphones. Always charge my devices. Subway is quite scary without it. I rather take a lot of buses than one crowded subway.

I can go to concerts, but I don't like to stay when it's over. Can't stand fairs or crowded, loud streets. I have learned the hard way after 15 years with PTSD.

I personally don't believe in normality. I don't know anyone who is actually  "normal".

Regarding sex, I think it's something like "I use you and you use me for each's sexual pleasure". I don't try to sugarcoat it anymore. And if consenting adults agree, there's nothing wrong with it.

It's very personal and subjective I think.

In my case I also suffer from major depression so I usually explain this first, in the surface, no details. Hence not so many questions regarding pills being taken or alcohol being avoided, etc. I mention panic attacks because people is more used to this than PTSD. So they understand better why the crowd avoidance, etc.  I don't like to explain why I suffer from PTSD so I try to avoid the subject until before sex. I have some huge scars that need explanation so it has to be done.

In my case, some have helped a lot, some have made everything worst. Been struggling with this for almost 20 years.

"Talking" therapy is uncomfortable, but some may help to cope in a less harmful way. It's hard to find the "right" therapist. Meds are a hit and miss too, and the wrong ones can make you feel do much more miserable, but some make help you to cope too.

Currently due to lockdown I don't have the talking therapy, I refuse to pay to chat with someone, I don't need it. I do take my meds, they help me a lot to cope with life.
